simple.meaning: שָׁעָה (shâʻâh) appears 15 times in the Hebrew Scriptures and is introduced in connection with flocks. The occurrence trail connects the name with an offering from the firstborn of the flock and its fat and divine acceptance. The surrounding account also brings the name into conflict.
simple.biblicalBackground: The first appearances are in Genesis, Exodus, 2 Samuel, Job, Psalms, and 1 more, beginning at Genesis 4:4. BibleIQ detects the main surrounding context as birth, flock, offering, firstborn, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שָׁעָה (H8159) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: People in Scripture are understood by their place in the story. BibleIQ follows שָׁעָה through the actual verses so the reader sees the person in context instead of as an isolated dictionary entry.
simple.summary: שָׁעָה (shâʻâh) / H8159 is tracked through Genesis 4:4, Genesis 4:5, Exodus 5:9, 2 Samuel 22:42. The entry is generated from source alignment, occurrence evidence, and the surrounding Scripture context.

definitions.short: to gaze at or about (properly, for help); by implication, to inspect , consider , compassionate , be nonplussed (as looking around in amazement) or bewildered
definitions.usage: depart, be dim, be dismayed, look (away), regard, have respect, spare, turn.

occurrences.englishText: Abel also brought some of the firstborn of his flock and of its fat. Yahweh respected Abel and his offering,
but he didn’t respect Cain and his offering. Cain was very angry, and the expression on his face fell.
Let heavier work be laid on the men, that they may labor in it. Don’t let them pay any attention to lying words.”
They looked, but there was no one to save;
How long will you not look away from me,
Look away from him, that he may rest,
Hold me up, and I will be safe,
In that day, people will look to their Maker, and their eyes will have respect for the Holy One of Israel.
They will not look to the altars, the work of their hands; neither shall they respect that which their fingers have made, either the Asherah poles, or the incense altars.
Therefore I said, “Look away from me. I will weep bitterly. Don’t labor to comfort me for the destruction of the daughter of my people.
Woe to those who go down to Egypt for help,
The eyes of those who see will not be dim,
Don’t you be afraid, for I am with you.
Declare the things that are to come hereafter,
